title: SSRIs Explained: How Antidepressants Work
description: Everything you need to know about SSRI medications. How they work, side effects, how long they take, and what to expect when starting or stopping.

content.text: SSRIs (selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors) are the most commonly prescribed antidepressants. Over 37 million Americans take them. But how do they actually work?

SSRIs increase serotonin availability in the brain by blocking its reabsorption (reuptake). This doesn't mean depression is simply 'low serotonin'—the reality is more complex. The increased serotonin triggers downstream changes in brain circuits and neuroplasticity.

items: Paroxetine (Paxil) - more sedating, harder to stop
Side effects often peak (nausea, headache, jitteriness)
This is normal and usually temporary
May notice slight improvements in energy or sleep
Full antidepressant effect not yet present
Mood, motivation, and thinking often improve
If no improvement by week 8, may need dose adjustment or different medication

content.text: Don't stop taking your SSRI because you feel better. This is a sign the medication is working. Stopping suddenly can cause withdrawal symptoms and relapse.

items: First episode: 6-12 months after feeling better
Three or more episodes: Consider long-term/indefinite
Always taper gradually under medical supervision

content.text: SSRIs aren't perfect, but they help millions of people. Give them adequate time to work (8+ weeks), communicate side effects to your doctor, and don't stop abruptly. They're one tool among many for treating depression and anxiety.
